title: Bounded rewind of the input head
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $s$ and $r$ be states, and let $d$ be an optional state. Suppose that every transition from $s$, regardless of the scanned symbols, moves the input head one position left and enters $r$; every transition from $r$ moves the head one position left and remains in $r$ when an input symbol is scanned, and moves it one position right and enters $d$ when no input symbol is scanned. From any configuration $c$ in state $s$, there is a time $t$ with $t \le p+2$, where $p$ is the input-head position of $c$, at which the machine is in state $d$ with input-head position $1$, and every other component of $c$ is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
States s and r and optional destination state d
Every transition from s moves the input head left and enters r, for all scanned symbols
From r, reading an input symbol moves left and remains in r
From r, reading no input symbol moves right and enters d
The initial configuration has state s
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with two distinguished
control states: a start state whose every transition moves the input head left and
enters a scan state, and a scan state that keeps moving left while it reads an input
symbol and, on reading the left boundary blank, moves right and enters a given
destination state. Then from any configuration $c$ in the start state there is a time
$t$ at most the input-head position of $c$ plus two after which the machine sits in the
destination state with input head at position one and every other component of $c$
unchanged.
